headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Dify can write shared state and egress broadly while Notion AI reads/writes workspace content, creating default-path leakage, conflict, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can write filesystem and process uploaded knowledge-base files, while Notion AI operates on shared workspace pages and team knowledge base content. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Notion content is copied into Dify or vice versa. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF content from Notion pages is pasted or imported into Dify prompts or knowledge files
IF Dify outputs are copied into Notion pages that later feed workspace Q&A
mitigations: Restrict imported Notion content to trusted sources only
Add a manual review step before copying agent outputs between systems
Use separate workspaces for raw inputs and generated outputs
Tag imported documents as untrusted and exclude them from agent prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch workspace content: Dify handles knowledge-base files and conversation logs, and Notion AI accesses pages and databases in the user’s workspace. Dify also has broad network egress, so sensitive workspace data can flow to external model providers if content is shared across the pair. The shared-workspace path is plausible in default use, but not proven to be uncontrolled.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is available in both the Dify knowledge base and the Notion workspace
IF Dify sends retrieved content to external model providers during generation
mitigations: Limit both agents to non-sensitive workspaces
Remove confidential files from Dify knowledge bases
Audit which pages Notion AI can access before use
Disable or narrow Dify tools that forward content externally
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on shared content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem and run shell/subprocesses, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted with no host execution but can act on shared workspace state. Their write surfaces differ, yet both can mutate overlapping knowledge artifacts, so concurrent edits can conflict even without direct OS-level contention. Uncertainty about exact synchronization pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same workspace-derived artifact within the same review window
IF Dify writes exported content back into a location Notion AI also treats as authoritative
mitigations: Assign one system as the source of truth per artifact
Avoid concurrent edits to the same document set
Use timestamped exports instead of in-place overwrites
Review diffs before syncing changes between systems
requires-engineering: add locking or merge resolution for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate agent/workflow outputs from tools and knowledge bases, and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, errors can propagate into summaries or actions. No evidence shows automatic action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Dify-generated text is inserted into Notion pages that later become authoritative workspace knowledge
IF Notion AI answers are reused by Dify workflows without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before reusing one agent’s output in the other
Keep generated drafts separate from source-of-truth pages
Add explicit citations or source links to reused content
Spot-check high-impact claims before publishing
requires-engineering: add verification gates between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify is open-source and self-hostable, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion-controlled backends and downstream model providers. That creates a likely retention/residency mismatch for the same data class, especially if sensitive workspace pages are processed by both. The profiles do not prove a specific legal breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound content is processed in both systems
IF the operator expects identical retention or deletion handling across Dify and Notion AI
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI and Dify shared flows
Document retention and deletion expectations for both systems
Use separate workspaces for regulated and non-regulated content
Review vendor data-processing terms before enabling sensitive content
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
